purpose: Texts of known origin, so the same rules can be run over all of them and the rates compared. This is variable-change evidence about these files. It is not a benchmark and nothing here measures accuracy.
construction: Human texts are fetched by scripts/fetch-corpus.mjs from the URL recorded on each entry and cut at a paragraph boundary near 1,500 words. Nothing in them is corrected, including Project Gutenberg's line wraps and its transcription of dashes.

Machine texts were written on 2026-09-19 by Claude Fable 5.1, the model that also wrote this linter, each in one pass from the prompt recorded on its entry. The prompt is verbatim. No machine text was edited after the linter was first run over it.

Known bias, stated plainly: the author of the machine texts had read the full rule list before writing them. That could push the plain samples toward the rules (the patterns were in mind) and makes the evasion sample a best case for evasion (the author knew exactly what to avoid). Samples from a model that has not seen the rules, and from other model families, would be better evidence. This corpus does not have them.
Factual claims inside the machine texts were not checked and must not be cited. The biography is fiction: every person, firm, bridge, paper and award in it is invented.

Hybrid texts are a human passage with one machine paragraph inserted, composed by scripts/build-corpus.mjs. machineLines is computed by that script and gives the inserted lines, so localisation can be checked.

files.prompt: Write one paragraph of about 120 words on the value of simple living, suitable for inserting into an essay about living deliberately.
files.machineText: In today's fast-paced world, the value of simple living has never been more relevant. By stripping away the unnecessary, we create space for what truly matters: meaningful relationships, personal growth, and a deeper connection to the natural world. Simple living is not about deprivation — it's about intention. It invites us to question the assumption that more is always better, and to recognize that true wealth lies not in possessions but in time, attention, and freedom. Studies show that people who embrace minimalism often report lower stress and greater life satisfaction. Ultimately, choosing simplicity is a powerful act of self-determination, serving as a reminder that a well-lived life is measured not by what we own, but by how fully we experience each day.

files.prompt: Write one paragraph of about 120 words explaining why factions are dangerous to popular government, suitable for inserting into an essay on the subject.
files.machineText: Factions pose a significant threat to popular government because they place the interests of a group above the common good. When citizens unite around a shared passion or interest that is adverse to the rights of others, the result is not only instability but also injustice. A majority faction is particularly dangerous, as it can leverage the very mechanisms of democracy to oppress minorities and undermine the rule of law. Moreover, factional conflict erodes public trust, fostering division and making compromise increasingly difficult. History offers numerous examples of republics that collapsed under the weight of internal strife, underscoring the importance of institutional safeguards. Ultimately, the challenge is not to eliminate factions, which would require destroying liberty itself, but to control their effects through a well-designed system of representation.
